headline: We have a proven short edge in falling markets but no live long edge, so this week we focus on validating long ideas, hardening shorts across regimes, and gathering the cheapest data that could unlock both

items.title: Test a long‑only contestant filtered to down‑wild regime
items.why: If a long signal can survive the same falling‑market regime where shorts thrive, it may reveal a hidden upside
items.how: Run a shadow account with the existing live referee, limiting trades to hours flagged as down‑wild; track hit‑rate and P&L

items.title: Add regime‑aware logic to the short contestant
items.why: Shorts already work in down markets; making the model explicitly switch on regime should keep performance when the market turns calmer
items.how: Create a variant that only activates when the regime detector says down‑calm or down‑wild, then run it in shadow

items.title: Gather funding‑rate and open‑interest series from Bybit and OKX
items.why: Extra funding signals can improve the model’s edge and help differentiate regimes without extra latency
items.how: Use the existing API collector to pull hourly funding and OI for the 40 coins, store for back‑test

items.title: Acquire a limited tick‑level order‑book snapshot for top 10 coins
items.why: Understanding true depth will let us verify that our hourly book isn’t being gamed and will improve execution risk assessment
items.how: Buy a one‑month tick‑level feed from a data vendor and ingest into the recorder

items.title: Build a simple on‑chain whale‑flow monitor
items.why: Large transfers often precede price moves; a cheap on‑chain signal could boost both long and short timing
items.how: Use the existing node to watch token transfer events for the 40 coins and flag spikes, then feed to the referee

note: A suggestion list only. Nothing here changes a setting or places a trade; the live race decides.
